title: Tate: a normal Noetherian domain complete along x with R/xR an N-2 domain is N-2
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $x\in R$. Assume (1) $R$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; (2) the quotient ring $R/xR$ is an integral domain and is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]; (3) $R$ is $xR$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], i.e. the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_nR/x^nR$ is bijective. Then $R$ is N-2: for every finite field extension $L$ [def-pc-field-extension] of the fraction field $K$ of $R$, the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589; which cites EGA 0_IV, Theorem 23.1.3), statement and proof

proof.text: Split the characteristic of K. In characteristic zero, finite-dimensional extensions are separable by Mathlib instances, and IsIntegralClosure.finite proves finiteness of the closure directly. No separably-generated-field definition or transcendence basis is used.
In positive prime characteristic apply isN2_of_finite_purelyInseparable_integralClosure and fix a finite purely inseparable extension L/K.

The private helper closure_hausdorff proves separatedness of S along x. If x=0, membership in xS forces the element to vanish. Otherwise for an element s in every x^nS choose q=p^e with s^q in K, using IsPurelyInseparable.pow_mem. Its integrality and normality place s^q in R. Writing s=x^nt gives t^q=s^q/x^(nq) in K, and normality puts t^q in R. Thus s^q belongs to every x^nR (since nq >= n), hence is zero by Hausdorffness of R. The domain L then gives s=0. These are the algebraic equalities and ideal-membership computations in the Lean helper.
Apply the closed-fibre lemma to obtain Module.Finite (R/xR) (S/xS).

Apply Module.finite_and_span_eq_top_of_adicComplete to the complete base R, the separated module S, and its finite reduction. This gives Module.Finite R S and completes the purely inseparable criterion.
